newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ledesma shifts sugar plan from Brazil to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Ledesma shifts sugar plan from Brazil to Argentina.

text.p: Argentine sugar firm Ledesma said Friday it will transfer a $100 million project from Brazil to Argentina after President Carlos Menem signs a sugar import tariffs bill already passed by Congress.

The bill maintains the current tariff scheme for sugar imports from members of the Mercosur customs union as long as "asymmetries due to the Brazilian sugar-alcohol system subsist," Ledesma told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.

"It is a very important step to define stable rules that allow competition on an equal footing," Ledesma said. Sugar production in Brazil is a by-product of the alcohol-fuel industry and Brazil subsidizes its sugar production, it added.
Argentine had a similar project but abandoned it due to its high fiscal cost, the company said.
As long as Brazil maintains its alcohol-fuel program, Argentina must maintain its tariff structure within a legal framework, Ledesma said.
It added once the national governmment signs the bill passed by Congress the firm will shift its investment project in Southern Brazil to northern Argentina's Jujuy province.
Ledesma said it had already told Jujuy governor Carlos Ferraro about the plans to initially invest more than $100 million over four years.
Mercosur is formed by Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.
